title: World Leaders Send Congratulations as India Marks 80th Independence Day
excerpt: From Washington to Singapore, heads of state hailed India's global partnerships as the country celebrated 80 years of freedom with diaspora events spanning three continents.
body:
• Heads of state from across the globe extended congratulations to India on its 80th Independence Day, hailing growing bilateral ties and strategic partnerships.
  • Prime Minister Modi thanked world leaders and led official celebrations at the Red Fort, where Vande Mataram was rendered for the first time during the Independence Day ceremony.
  • Indian communities in the US, Singapore, and elsewhere held large-scale celebrations, with US Pacific Northwest leaders joining festivities in Seattle.
  • The diplomatic outpouring reflects India's expanded global footprint under a decade of intensified international engagement.

World leaders from Washington to Moscow extended warm congratulations to India on Friday as the country celebrated its 80th Independence Day, marking eight decades since gaining freedom from British colonial rule on August 15, 1947.

A Global Chorus of Greetings

The messages poured in from across the geopolitical spectrum. French President Emmanuel Macron was among the first Western leaders to congratulate India, continuing a pattern of deepening Indo-French strategic ties that has included defence cooperation, nuclear energy partnerships, and climate initiatives. Russian President Vladimir Putin praised India's achievements in socio-economic and scientific fields, emphasising the "special, privileged strategic partnership" between Moscow and New Delhi.

Leaders from India's immediate neighbourhood — including Bhutan, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives — also sent messages highlighting regional bonds. PM Modi responded to each, thanking them and reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening partnerships, according to the Prime Minister's Office.

Diaspora Celebrations Span Continents

Indian communities abroad marked the milestone with parades, flag-hoisting ceremonies, and cultural events. In Seattle, US Pacific Northwest leaders joined India's 80th Independence Day celebrations, reflecting the growing political influence of the Indian-American community, which now numbers over five million. The event underscored how Indian Independence Day has become a fixture in the American civic calendar, particularly in states with large diaspora populations like Washington, California, New Jersey, and Texas.

In Singapore, the Indian envoy led official celebrations attended by hundreds of community members and diplomatic corps representatives. Similar events took place across the UK, Canada, Australia, and the Gulf states, where large Indian expatriate communities gathered to mark the occasion.

India at 80: A Different Global Player

The breadth of diplomatic greetings reflects how significantly India's international standing has shifted. When India marked its 50th Independence Day in 1997, it was a regional power still emerging from economic liberalisation. At 75 in 2022, it was hosting the G20 presidency and positioning itself as a voice for the Global South.

At 80, India is the world's fifth-largest economy, a major defence exporter, and a central player in global conversations about technology, climate, and trade. The congratulatory messages from leaders spanning the Americas, Europe, Asia, and Africa illustrate the extent of India's diplomatic reach — a reach that was far less automatic a decade ago.

Red Fort Ceremony Marks a First

In New Delhi, PM Modi led the official ceremony at the Red Fort, where Vande Mataram was rendered during the Independence Day celebration for the first time. The ceremony featured cultural performances and patriotic displays as India reflected on eight decades of democratic governance and charted its vision for the centenary in 2047.
